title.zh: 卷四百〇三 列傳第一百六十二 趙方 賈涉 扈再興 孟宗政 張威
title.en: Volume 403 Biographies 162: Zhao Fang, Jia She, Hu Zaixing, Meng Zongzheng, Zhang Wei
title.raw: 卷四百〇三 列傳第一百六十二 趙方 賈涉 扈再興 孟宗政 張威 Volume 403 Biographies 162: Zhao Fang, Jia She, Hu Zaixing, Meng Zongzheng, Zhang Wei

sentences.zh: 趙方，字彥直，衡山人。

translations.literal: Zhao Fang, courtesy name Yanzhi, was a native of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fang, styled Yanzhi, came from Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 父棠，少從胡宏學，慷慨有大志。

translations.literal: His father Tang, in youth studied under Hu Hong, was generous in spirit and had great ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tang had studied under Hu Hong in his youth; he was generous in spirit and possessed great ambitions.

sentences.zh: 嘗見張浚於督府，浚雅敬其才，欲以右選官之，棠不為屈。

translations.literal: Once he met Zhang Jun at the supervisory headquarters; Jun greatly respected his talent and wished to appoint him to an office in the right selection category, but Tang would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: He once met Zhang Jun at the military headquarters. Zhang Jun held his talent in high regard and wanted to appoint him to an office in the right selection category, but Tang would not compromise his principles.

sentences.zh: 累以策言兵事，浚奇之，命子栻與棠交，方遂從栻學。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he submitted memorials discussing military affairs; Jun marvelled at this, ordered his son Shi to befriend Tang, and Fang then studied under Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted policy proposals on military affairs. Zhang Jun was impressed and had his son Zhang Shi become friends with Tang; Zhao Fang then went on to study under Zhang Shi.

sentences.zh: 淳熙八年舉進士，調蒲圻尉，疑獄多所委決。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chunxi he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Puqi, and many doubtful cases were entrusted to his decision.
translations.idiomatic: In 1181, the eighth year of Chunxi, he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as assistant magistrate of Puqi, where many difficult legal cases were entrusted to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 授大寧監教授，俗陋甚，方擇可教者親訓誘之，人皆感勵，自是始有進士。

translations.literal: Appointed professor at the Daning Supervisorate; customs were very crude; Fang selected those who could be taught and personally instructed and guided them; all were moved and encouraged, and from then on there were jinshi degree holders.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at the Daning salt supervisorate, where local customs were exceedingly crude. Fang selected students who showed promise and personally taught and guided them; people were moved and inspired, and from then on the region produced jinshi graduates.

sentences.zh: 知青陽縣，告其守史彌遠曰：「催科不擾，是催科中撫字；

translations.literal: Serving as magistrate of Qingyang County, he told his superior Shi Miyuan: "Tax collection without disturbance is nurturing the people within tax collection;
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Qingyang County, he told his superior Shi Miyuan: "Collecting taxes without harassing the people is nurturing the people even amid tax collection;

sentences.zh: 刑罰無差，是刑罰中教化。

translations.literal: Punishments without error are moral cultivation within punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Applying punishments without error is teaching moral values even through the administration of punishment."

sentences.zh: 」人以為名言。

translations.literal: People regarded it as a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: People regarded these as words of lasting wisdom.

sentences.zh: 主管江西安撫司機宜文字，京湖帥李大性辟知隨州。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer of the Jiangxi Pacification Commission; Li Daxing, commander of Jing-Hu, summoned him to serve as prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a staff officer on the Jiangxi Pacification Commission. Li Daxing, commander of the Jing-Hu circuit, recruited him to serve as prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 南北初講和，旱蝗相仍，方親走四郊以禱，一夕大雨，蝗盡死，歲大熟。

translations.literal: North and south had just made peace; drought and locusts followed one after another; Fang personally went to the four suburbs to pray; in one night a great rain fell, the locusts all died, and the year brought a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Right after the north-south peace was concluded, drought and locust plagues struck in succession. Fang personally went out to the four suburbs to pray, and in a single night heavy rain fell, the locusts all perished, and that year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 適和議成，諸郡寖弛備，方獨招兵擇將，拔土豪孟宗政等補以官。

translations.literal: Just as the peace agreement was concluded, various prefectures gradually relaxed their defenses; Fang alone recruited troops and selected generals, promoting local strongmen such as Meng Zongzheng and appointing them to office.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the peace treaty took effect, prefectures across the region gradually slackened their defenses. Fang alone set about recruiting soldiers and selecting commanders, promoting local strongmen such as Meng Zongzheng and appointing them to official posts.

sentences.zh: 提舉京西常平兼轉運判官、提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He served as commissioner of the Jingxi Ever-Normal Granaries, concurrently as transport vice-commissioner and judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner of the Jingxi Ever-Normal Granaries, concurrently serving as vice transport commissioner and judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 時劉光祖以耆德為帥，方事以師禮，自言：「吾性太剛，每見劉公，使人更和緩。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Guangzu, as an elder of virtue, was commander; Fang treated him with the rites due a teacher and said himself: "My nature is too hard; every time I see Lord Liu, it makes one more mild and gentle.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Guangzu, revered for his seniority and virtue, served as circuit commander. Fang treated him with the respect due a teacher and said of himself: "My temperament is too rigid; every time I see Lord Liu, I find myself becoming more calm and measured.

sentences.zh: 」嘗請光祖書 「勤謹和緩」四字，揭坐隅以為戒。

translations.literal: Once he asked Guangzu to write the four characters "diligent, careful, harmonious, and gentle," and displayed them in a corner of his seat as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Liu Guangzu to write the four characters "Diligent, Careful, Harmonious, and Gentle" and posted them in a corner of his chair as a constant reminder.

sentences.zh: 以金部員外郎召，尋加直秘閣，改湖北轉運判官兼知鄂州。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Gold Department; soon given direct appointment to the Secretariat Archive; changed to Hubei transport vice-commissioner concurrently serving as prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Gold Department, and soon after was given direct appointment to the Secretariat Archive. He was then reassigned as Hubei transport vice-commissioner while concurrently serving as prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 升直煥章閣兼權江陵府，增修三海八匱，以壯形勢。

translations.literal: Promoted to direct appointment to the Hall of Glorious Culture, concurrently acting as administrator of Jiangling Prefecture; expanded and repaired the Three Seas and Eight Caches to strengthen the strategic position.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct appointment to the Hall of Glorious Culture and concurrently appointed acting administrator of Jiangling Prefecture, where he expanded and repaired the Three Seas and Eight Caches to strengthen the region's strategic posture.

sentences.zh: 進秘閣修撰、知江陵府、主管湖北安撫司事兼權荊湖置司。

translations.literal: Advanced to Compiler of the Secretariat Archive, administrator of Jiangling Prefecture, director of Hubei Pacification Commission affairs, concurrently acting head of the established Jing-Hu headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler of the Secretariat Archive and appointed administrator of Jiangling Prefecture, placed in charge of the Hubei Pacification Commission and concurrently acting as head of the established Jing-Hu headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時金偪於兵，計其必南徙，日夜為備。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin were pressed by warfare; Fang calculated that they would certainly move south and prepared day and night.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jin were hard pressed by war, and Fang calculated that they would inevitably push southward; he made preparations day and night.

sentences.zh: 荊門有東西兩山險要，方築堡其上，增戍兵以遏其衝。

translations.literal: At Jingmen there were eastern and western mountains that were strategically vital; Fang built fortresses on them and increased garrison troops to block the enemy's line of advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingmen, the eastern and western mountains were strategically vital. Fang built fortresses on them and increased the garrison to block the enemy's line of advance.

sentences.zh: 進右文殿修撰。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 金樊快明謀歸宋，追兵至襄陽，方遣孟宗政、扈再興以百騎邀之，殺千餘人，金人遁去。

translations.literal: The Jin subject Fan Kuaiming plotted to defect to Song; pursuing troops reached Xiangyang; Fang sent Meng Zongzheng and Hu Zaixing with a hundred horsemen to intercept them, killed more than a thousand men, and the Jin forces fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin subject Fan Kuaiming plotted to defect to Song, and pursuing Jin troops reached Xiangyang. Fang sent Meng Zongzheng and Hu Zaixing with a hundred horsemen to intercept them, killed more than a thousand men, and the Jin forces fled.

sentences.zh: 權工部侍郎、寶謨閣待制、京湖制置使兼知襄陽府。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Works, Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Precious Instruction, Jing-Hu military commissioner concurrently serving as prefect of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Vice Minister of Works and Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Precious Instruction, as Jing-Hu military commissioner while concurrently serving as prefect of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 諜知金人決意犯境，乃下防夏之令。

translations.literal: Spies learned that the Jin had decided to invade the border, and he then issued orders for summer defense.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reports revealed that the Jin had decided to invade the border, and he then issued orders for summer defense.

sentences.zh: 金相高琪及其樞密烏古倫慶壽犯陳、光化、隨、棗理、信陽、均州，方夜半呼其子范、葵曰：「朝廷和戰之說未定，觀此益亂人意，吾策決矣，惟有提兵臨邊決戰以報國耳。

translations.literal: The Jin chancellor Gao Qi and his Privy Council member Wugulun Qingshou attacked Chen, Guanghua, Suizhou, Zaoli, Xinyang, and Junzhou; at midnight Fang summoned his sons Fan and Kui and said: "The court has not yet decided between peace and war; seeing this only further unsettles people's minds. My plan is settled: I have only to lead troops to the border and fight a decisive battle to repay the state."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin chancellor Gao Qi and his Privy Council member Wugulun Qingshou attacked Chen, Guanghua, Suizhou, Zaoli, Xinyang, and Junzhou. At midnight Fang summoned his sons Fan and Kui and said: "The court has not yet decided between peace and war, and scenes like this only unsettle people further. My mind is made up: I have only to lead troops to the border and fight a decisive battle to repay my debt to the state."

sentences.zh: 」遂抗疏主戰，親往襄陽。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial advocating war and personally went to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial advocating war and personally went to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 金人圍棗陽急，方遣宗政、再興等援棗陽，仍增戍光化、信陽、均州，以聯聲勢。

translations.literal: The Jin forces were pressing the siege of Zaoyang; Fang sent Zongzheng, Zaixing, and others to relieve Zaoyang, and also increased the garrisons at Guanghua, Xinyang, and Junzhou to coordinate their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin forces were pressing the siege of Zaoyang. Fang sent Zongzheng, Zaixing, and others to relieve Zaoyang, and also reinforced the garrisons at Guanghua, Xinyang, and Junzhou to coordinate their strength.

sentences.zh: 已而棗陽守趙觀敗金人於城外，再興、宗政至，與觀夾擊，又敗之，棗陽圍解。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zaoyang's defender Zhao Guan defeated the Jin outside the city; Zaixing and Zongzheng arrived and, together with Guan, attacked from both sides and defeated them again; the siege of Zaoyang was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zaoyang's defender Zhao Guan defeated the Jin outside the city. When Zaixing and Zongzheng arrived, they joined Guan in a pincer attack and defeated the enemy again, lifting the siege of Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 方申飭諸將，當遏於境上，不可使之入而後拒之於城下。

translations.literal: Fang repeatedly admonished the generals that they must stop the enemy at the border and must not let them enter and only then resist them beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Fang repeatedly admonished his generals that they must stop the enemy at the border and must not allow them to penetrate deep inside before offering resistance beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 時麥正熟，方遣兵護民刈之，令清野以俟。

translations.literal: At the time the wheat was just ripe; Fang sent troops to protect the people in harvesting it and ordered a scorched-earth policy while waiting.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the wheat was just ripening. Fang sent troops to protect the people as they harvested it and ordered a scorched-earth policy while awaiting the enemy.

sentences.zh: 再疏力陳不可和者七，戰議遂定。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial forcefully setting forth seven reasons why peace was impossible, and the decision for war was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial forcefully setting forth seven reasons why peace was impossible, and the decision for war was then settled.

sentences.zh: 金將完顏賽不入境，兵號十萬。

translations.literal: The Jin general Wanyan Saibuo entered the border; his army was said to number one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wanyan Saibuo crossed the border with an army said to number one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 方部分諸將，金人犯棗陽者，宗政敗之於尚家川；

translations.literal: Fang deployed the various generals: where the Jin attacked Zaoyang, Zongzheng defeated them at Shangjiachuan;
translations.idiomatic: Fang deployed his generals accordingly: where the Jin attacked Zaoyang, Zongzheng defeated them at Shangjiachuan;

sentences.zh: 犯隨州者，劉世興敗之於磨子平。

translations.literal: where they attacked Suizhou, Liu Shixing defeated them at Moziping.
translations.idiomatic: where they attacked Suizhou, Liu Shixing defeated them at Moziping.

sentences.zh: 相持逾年，方調世興移師，與許國、再興援棗陽；

translations.literal: After more than a year of stalemate, Fang ordered Shixing to transfer his army and, together with Xu Guo and Zaixing, relieve Zaoyang;
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year of stalemate, Fang ordered Shixing to transfer his army and, together with Xu Guo and Zaixing, relieve Zaoyang;

sentences.zh: 張興、李雄韜援隨州。

translations.literal: Zhang Xing and Li Xiongtao relieved Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing and Li Xiongtao relieved Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 隨州圍解，再興等轉戰入棗陽。

translations.literal: The siege of Suizhou was lifted, and Zaixing and the others fought their way into Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Suizhou was lifted, and Zaixing and the others fought their way into Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 時宗政守城，伏兵城東，金人遇伏敗走。

translations.literal: At the time Zongzheng was defending the city; he hid troops east of the city, and the Jin, encountering the ambush, were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zongzheng was defending the city. He hid troops east of the city, and when the Jin encountered the ambush they were defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 未幾再至，再興又敗之，自是無日不戰。

translations.literal: Before long they came again; Zaixing defeated them again, and from then on there was fighting every day.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jin returned; Zaixing defeated them again, and from then on there was fighting every day.

sentences.zh: 金人三面來攻，宗政出東門，再興出南門，世興出北門，大合戰敗之。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked from three sides; Zongzheng went out the east gate, Zaixing the south gate, and Shixing the north gate; they joined battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin attacked from three sides. Zongzheng went out the east gate, Zaixing the south gate, and Shixing the north gate; they joined in a great battle and defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 金人朝進莫退，力不能捍；

translations.literal: The Jin advanced by day and did not retreat; their strength could not be withstood;
translations.idiomatic: The Jin advanced by day and would not retreat; their strength could not be withstood;

sentences.zh: 諸將表裏合謀，國自南山進，張威自瀼河進，世興、李琪出城與國會，再興出城與威會，掎角追擊，金人遂潰。

translations.literal: the generals conspired inside and out: Guo advanced from the south mountain, Zhang Wei from the Rang River, Shixing and Li Qi went out of the city to join Guo, Zaixing went out to join Wei, and in pincer formation they pursued and attacked; the Jin then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: the generals coordinated an inside-outside plan: Guo advanced from the south mountain, Zhang Wei from the Rang River, Shixing and Li Qi sallied from the city to join Guo, Zaixing sallied to join Wei, and in pincer formation they pursued and attacked until the Jin forces collapsed.

sentences.zh: 光化守潘景伯亦設伏敗金人於趙家橋，孟宗德又破之於隨州鴨兒山，擒賽不妻弟王醜漢，金人遂誅賽不。

translations.literal: Guanghua's defender Pan Jingbo also set an ambush and defeated the Jin at Zhaoqiao Bridge; Meng Zongde again broke them at Yao'ershan in Suizhou and captured Saibuo's wife's younger brother Wang Chouhan; the Jin then executed Saibuo.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua's defender Pan Jingbo also set an ambush and defeated the Jin at Zhaoqiao Bridge. Meng Zongde broke them again at Yao'ershan in Suizhou and captured Saibuo's wife's younger brother Wang Chouhan, after which the Jin executed Saibuo.

sentences.zh: 方以功遷龍圖閣待制，封長沙縣男，賜食邑。

translations.literal: For his achievements Fang was promoted to Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, enfeoffed as Baron of Changsha County, and granted a fief of sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements Fang was promoted to Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, enfeoffed as Baron of Changsha County, and granted a fief of sustenance.

sentences.zh: 金人復大舉，命訛可圍棗陽，塹其外，繞以土城。

translations.literal: The Jin again mounted a major campaign, ordering Eke to besiege Zaoyang, digging trenches outside it and encircling it with an earthen wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin again mounted a major campaign, ordering Eke to besiege Zaoyang, digging trenches outside the city and encircling it with an earthen wall.

sentences.zh: 方計其空巢穴而來，若搗其虛，則棗陽之圍自解。

translations.literal: Fang calculated that they had come with their nests emptied; if one struck their rear, the siege of Zaoyang would resolve itself.
translations.idiomatic: Fang calculated that they had come with their rear areas stripped bare; if one struck their vulnerable rear, the siege of Zaoyang would resolve itself.

sentences.zh: 乃命國東向唐州，再興西向鄧州，又命子范監軍，葵後殿。

translations.literal: He then ordered Guo east toward Tangzhou, Zaixing west toward Dengzhou, and also ordered his son Fan to supervise the army with Kui in the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Guo east toward Tangzhou and Zaixing west toward Dengzhou, and also placed his son Fan in command of the army with Kui covering the rear.

sentences.zh: 時宗政在城中，日夜鏖戰，焚其攻具，金人不敢近城。

translations.literal: At the time Zongzheng was in the city fighting day and night; he burned their siege engines, and the Jin did not dare approach the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zongzheng was in the city fighting day and night. He burned the enemy siege engines, and the Jin did not dare approach the walls.

sentences.zh: 西師由光化境出，砦於三尖山，拔順陽縣，金人率眾仰攻，大敗。

translations.literal: The western army emerged from Guanghua territory, encamped at Sanjianshan, captured Shunyang County, and when the Jin massed troops to attack uphill they were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The western army emerged from Guanghua territory, encamped at Sanjianshan, and captured Shunyang County. When the Jin massed troops to attack uphill, they were routed.

sentences.zh: 再興與國兩道並進，掠唐、鄧境，焚其城柵糧儲。

translations.literal: Zaixing and Guo advanced on two routes, raiding the Tang and Deng territories and burning their fortifications, stockades, and grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing and Guo advanced on two routes, raiding the Tang and Deng territories and burning enemy fortifications, stockades, and grain stores.

sentences.zh: 棗陽城堅，金頓兵八十餘日，方知其氣已竭，乃召國、再興還，併東師隸於再興，尅期合戰。

translations.literal: Zaoyang's walls were strong; the Jin halted their army for more than eighty days; Fang knew their spirit was exhausted and then summoned Guo and Zaixing back, placing the eastern army under Zaixing's command and setting a date for a combined battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zaoyang's walls were strong, and the Jin halted their army for more than eighty days. When Fang saw that their fighting spirit was exhausted, he summoned Guo and Zaixing back, placed the eastern army under Zaixing's command, and set a date for a combined battle.

sentences.zh: 再興敗金人於瀼河，又敗之城南，宗政自城中出夾擊，殺其眾三萬，金人大潰，訛可單騎遁，獲其貲糧、器甲不可勝計。

translations.literal: Zaixing defeated the Jin at the Rang River and again defeated them south of the city; Zongzheng sallied from the city in a pincer attack and killed thirty thousand of their men; the Jin collapsed in rout; Eke fled alone on horseback; their wealth, grain, weapons, and armor captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing defeated the Jin at the Rang River and again south of the city. Zongzheng sallied from the city in a pincer attack, killing thirty thousand of their men. The Jin collapsed in rout; Eke fled alone on horseback, and the wealth, grain, weapons, and armor captured were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 進方煥章閣直學士。

translations.literal: Fang was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Glorious Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Glorious Culture.

sentences.zh: 奏乞均官軍民兵廩給，自備馬者倍之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting equal rations for regular troops and militia, with double rations for those who supplied their own horses.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting equal rations for regular troops and militia, with double rations for those who supplied their own horses.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「使民兵夏歸，以省月給，秋復詣屯守禦。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Let the militia return home in summer to save monthly pay, and in autumn assemble again for garrison defense."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Let the militia return home in summer to save monthly pay, and in autumn assemble again for garrison defense."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 方料金人數不得志於棗陽，必將同時並攻諸城，當先發以制之。

translations.literal: Fang calculated that since the Jin had failed to achieve their aim at Zaoyang, they would certainly attack the various cities simultaneously, and one should strike first to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang calculated that since the Jin had failed to achieve their aim at Zaoyang, they would certainly attack multiple cities simultaneously, and one should strike first to seize the initiative.

sentences.zh: 命國、宗政出師向唐，再興向鄧，戒之曰：「毋深入，毋攻城，第潰其保甲，燬其城砦，空其貲糧而已。

translations.literal: He ordered Guo and Zongzheng to lead armies toward Tang, Zaixing toward Deng, and warned them: "Do not penetrate deeply, do not besiege cities; only break up their local defense units, burn their fortifications and stockades, and empty their wealth and grain."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Guo and Zongzheng to lead armies toward Tang and Zaixing toward Deng, and warned them: "Do not penetrate deeply and do not besiege cities; only break up their local defense units, burn their fortifications and stockades, and empty their stores of wealth and grain."

sentences.zh: 」宗政進破湖陽縣，擒其千戶趙興兒；

translations.literal: Zongzheng advanced and captured Huyang County, seizing their chiliarch Zhao Xing'er;
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng advanced and captured Huyang County, seizing their chiliarch Zhao Xing'er;

sentences.zh: 國遣部將耶律均與金人戰於北陽，戮其將李提控；

translations.literal: Guo sent his subordinate Yelü Jun to fight the Jin at Beiyang and killed their commander Li Tikong;
translations.idiomatic: Guo sent his subordinate Yelü Jun to fight the Jin at Beiyang and killed their commander Li Tikong;

sentences.zh: 再興破高頭城，大敗金兵，遂薄鄧州。

translations.literal: Zaixing captured Gaotou City, greatly defeated the Jin army, and then pressed close to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing captured Gaotou City, routed the Jin army, and then pressed close to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐州兵來援，迎敗之，降者踵至。

translations.literal: Tangzhou sent troops to relieve them and was met and defeated; surrenderers arrived in an unbroken stream.
translations.idiomatic: Tangzhou sent troops to relieve the city and was met and defeated; surrenderers arrived in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 已而金兵至樊城，方命再興陣以待之，方視其師；

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jin troops reached Fancheng; Fang ordered Zaixing to form battle lines and await them, and personally inspected his army;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jin troops reached Fancheng. Fang ordered Zaixing to form battle lines and await them, and personally inspected his army;

sentences.zh: 金人三日不敢動，遂遁。

translations.literal: for three days the Jin did not dare move and then fled.
translations.idiomatic: for three days the Jin did not dare move and then fled.

sentences.zh: 金將駙馬阿海犯淮西，樞密完顏小驢屯唐州為後繼。

translations.literal: The Jin general the imperial son-in-law Ahai invaded Huai West; Privy Council member Wanyan Xiaolü encamped at Tangzhou as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general, the imperial son-in-law Ahai, invaded Huai West, while Privy Council member Wanyan Xiaolü encamped at Tangzhou as rear support.

sentences.zh: 方先攻唐伐其謀，及使再興發棗陽兵擊其西，國發桐栢兵擊其東。

translations.literal: Fang first attacked Tangzhou to disrupt their plan, and also ordered Zaixing to lead Zaoyang troops to strike their west and Guo to lead Tongbai troops to strike their east.
translations.idiomatic: Fang first attacked Tangzhou to disrupt their plan, and also ordered Zaixing to lead Zaoyang troops to strike their west and Guo to lead Tongbai troops to strike their east.

sentences.zh: 再興敗金人於唐城，斬小驢，圍其城五匝，垂下。

translations.literal: Zaixing defeated the Jin at Tangcheng, beheaded Xiaolü, and surrounded the city on five sides, pressing the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing defeated the Jin at Tangcheng, beheaded Xiaolü, and surrounded the city on five sides, pressing the siege.

sentences.zh: 會蘄、黃繼陷，詔趣方遣救，方亟命國保鄂，再興援淮西。

translations.literal: Just then Qi and Huang fell in succession; an edict urgently ordered Fang to dispatch relief; Fang immediately ordered Guo to defend Ezhou and Zaixing to relieve Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Qi and Huang fell in succession. An edict urgently ordered Fang to dispatch relief, and he immediately ordered Guo to defend Ezhou and Zaixing to relieve Huai West.

sentences.zh: 國還鄂州保江；

translations.literal: Guo returned to Ezhou to defend the river;
translations.idiomatic: Guo returned to Ezhou to defend the river;

sentences.zh: 再興軍至蘄之靈山，伺金人歸而擊之，土豪祝文蔚橫突入陣，金人大敗，國遣張寶將兵來會，李全等兵亦至，金人遂潰，再興追逐六十里，擒其監軍合答。

translations.literal: Zaixing's army reached Lingshan in Qi, waited for the Jin to withdraw and then struck them; the local strongman Zhu Wenwei charged into the formation; the Jin were greatly defeated; Guo sent Zhang Bao with troops to join them, Li Quan's troops also arrived, the Jin collapsed, and Zaixing pursued for sixty li and captured their supervising general Heda.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing's army reached Lingshan in Qi and waited for the Jin to withdraw before striking them. The local strongman Zhu Wenwei charged into the enemy formation, the Jin were routed, Guo sent Zhang Bao with troops to join the fight, Li Quan's forces also arrived, the Jin collapsed, and Zaixing pursued for sixty li and captured their supervising general Heda.

sentences.zh: 進方顯謨閣直學士、太中大夫、權刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Fang was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Instruction, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and Acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Instruction, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, and Acting Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 俄得疾，進徽猷閣學士、京湖制置大使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he fell ill and was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Imperial Instruction and Great Military Commissioner of Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he fell ill and was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Imperial Instruction and Great Military Commissioner of Jing-Hu.

sentences.zh: 歸還，力疾犒師，第其功上之。

translations.literal: Returning home, he forced himself despite illness to reward the troops and ranked their achievements for submission to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On returning home, he forced himself despite illness to reward the troops and ranked their achievements for submission to the throne.

sentences.zh: 病革，曰：「未死一日，當立一日紀綱。

translations.literal: As his illness became critical he said: "For every day I have not died, I must uphold discipline for one day.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness became critical he said: "For every day I have not died, I must uphold discipline for one day.

sentences.zh: 」引再興臥內，勉以協心報國。

translations.literal: He summoned Zaixing into his private chamber and urged him to cooperate in repaying the state.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Zaixing into his private chamber and urged him to cooperate wholeheartedly in repaying their debt to the state.

sentences.zh: 貽書宰相，論疆場大計。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to the chief councillor discussing the great plan for the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a letter to the chief councillor discussing the great strategic plan for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 是夕有大星隕於襄陽。

translations.literal: That night a great star fell at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: That night a great star fell over Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 以端明殿學士、正議大夫致仕，贈銀青光祿大夫，累贈太師，諡「忠肅」。

translations.literal: He was granted retirement as Direct Academician of the Hall of Sagacious Brightness and Grand Master of Direct Remonstrance; posthumously awarded Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace, cumulatively posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor, and given the posthumous title "Loyal and Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: He was granted retirement as Direct Academician of the Hall of Sagacious Brightness and Grand Master of Direct Remonstrance; posthumously awarded Silver-Gleam Grand Master of the Palace, later promoted posthumously to Grand Preceptor, and given the posthumous title "Loyal and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 方起自儒生，帥邊十年，以戰為守，合官民兵為一體，通制總司為一家。

translations.literal: Fang rose from the ranks of scholar-officials, commanded the frontier for ten years, used warfare as defense, united regular troops and militia into one body, and made the overall command system one household.
translations.idiomatic: Fang rose from the ranks of scholar-officials and commanded the frontier for ten years. He used active warfare as his form of defense, united regular troops and militia into a single force, and integrated the overall command system into one cohesive whole.

sentences.zh: 持軍嚴，每令諸將飲酒勿醉，當使日日可戰。

translations.literal: He held the army strictly; every time he ordered the generals to drink wine he told them not to become drunk, so that they would be fit to fight every day.
translations.idiomatic: He held the army to strict discipline. Whenever he allowed his generals to drink wine, he told them not to become drunk, so that they would remain fit to fight every day.

sentences.zh: 淮、蜀沿邊屢遭金人之禍，而京西一境獨全。

translations.literal: Along the Huai and Shu frontiers there were repeated calamities from the Jin, but the Jingxi region alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Huai and Shu frontiers there were repeated calamities at the hands of the Jin, but the Jingxi region alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 嘗問相業於劉清之，清之以留意人才對。

translations.literal: Once he asked Liu Qingzhi about the art of serving as chief minister; Qingzhi answered by saying one should attend to talent.
translations.idiomatic: Once he asked Liu Qingzhi about the art of serving as chief minister, and Qingzhi answered that one should attend to nurturing talent.

sentences.zh: 故知名士如陳晐、游九功輩皆拔為大吏，諸名將多在其麾下。

translations.literal: Therefore renowned scholars such as Chen Gai and You Jiugong were all promoted to high office, and many famous generals served under him.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, renowned scholars such as Chen Gai and You Jiugong were all promoted to high office, and many famous generals served under his command.

sentences.zh: 若扈再興、孟宗政皆起自土豪，推誠擢任，致其死力，藩屏一方，使朝廷無北顧之憂。

translations.literal: Men such as Hu Zaixing and Meng Zongzheng had risen from local strongmen; he promoted them with sincerity and entrusted them with office, bringing them to exert themselves to the death; they shielded one region and kept the court from worry over the north.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Hu Zaixing and Meng Zongzheng had risen from the ranks of local strongmen. Fang promoted them with sincerity and entrusted them with command, winning their utmost loyalty; they shielded the region and spared the court worry over the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 故其沒也，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: Therefore when he died, everyone regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when he died, everyone regretted his loss.

sentences.zh: 子：董、薿、范、葵。

translations.literal: Sons: Dong, Ni, Fan, and Kui.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Dong, Ni, Fan, and Kui.

sentences.zh: 范、葵有傳。

translations.literal: Fan and Kui have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Kui have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 賈涉，字濟川，天台人。

translations.literal: Jia She, courtesy name Jichuan, was a native of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Jia She, styled Jichuan, came from Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 幼好讀古書，慷慨有大志。

translations.literal: In youth he loved reading ancient books and was generous in spirit with great ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved reading ancient books and was generous in spirit with great ambitions.

sentences.zh: 以父任高郵尉，改萬安丞。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege he became assistant magistrate of Gaoyou, then was changed to vice magistrate of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's yin privilege he became assistant magistrate of Gaoyou, then was reassigned as vice magistrate of Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 寶應擇令，堂差涉至邑，請城之。

translations.literal: Baoying selected a magistrate; the court dispatched She to the district, and he requested that walls be built.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoying needed a magistrate, the court dispatched She to the district, and he requested that city walls be built.

sentences.zh: 役興，以憂去。

translations.literal: When the labor was begun, he resigned out of grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the labor project was begun, he resigned out of grief.

sentences.zh: 金人犯光州，起涉竟前役。

translations.literal: The Jin invaded Guangzhou; She was recalled to complete the earlier project.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded Guangzhou, She was recalled to complete the earlier project.

sentences.zh: 通判真州，改大理司直、知盱眙軍。

translations.literal: He served as vice prefect of Zhenzhou, then was changed to Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review and administrator of Xuyi Military Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Zhenzhou, then was reassigned as Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review and administrator of Xuyi Military Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淮人季先、沈鐸說楚州守應純之以招山東人，純之令鐸遣周用和說楊友、劉全、李全等以其眾至，先招石珪、葛平、楊德廣，通號「忠義軍」。

translations.literal: The Huai native Ji Xian and Shen Duo persuaded Chuzhou's defender Ying Chunzhi to recruit people from Shandong; Chunzhi ordered Duo to send Zhou Yonghe to persuade Yang You, Liu Quan, Li Quan, and others to bring their followers; first they recruited Shi Gui, Ge Ping, and Yang Deguang, collectively called the "Loyal and Righteous Army."
translations.idiomatic: The Huai native Ji Xian and Shen Duo persuaded Chuzhou's defender Ying Chunzhi to recruit people from Shandong. Chunzhi ordered Duo to send Zhou Yonghe to persuade Yang You, Liu Quan, Li Quan, and others to bring their followers. They first recruited Shi Gui, Ge Ping, and Yang Deguang, who collectively became known as the "Loyal and Righteous Army."

sentences.zh: 珪等反，斃鐸於漣水，純之罷，通判梁丙行守事，欲省其糧使自潰。

translations.literal: Gui and the others rebelled, killed Duo at Lianshui, Chunzhi was dismissed, Vice Prefect Liang Bing acted as defender, and wished to cut their rations to make them collapse of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and the others rebelled and killed Duo at Lianshui. Chunzhi was dismissed, Vice Prefect Liang Bing acted as defender, and wished to cut their rations to make them collapse of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 珪、德廣等以漣水諸軍度淮屯南渡門，焚掠幾盡。

translations.literal: Gui, Deguang, and the others led the Lianshui armies across the Huai to encamp at Nandu Gate and burned and plundered almost everything.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, Deguang, and the others led the Lianshui armies across the Huai to encamp at Nandu Gate and burned and plundered almost everything.

sentences.zh: 謂：「朝廷欲和殘金，置我軍何地？

translations.literal: They said: "The court wishes to make peace with the remnant Jin — where does that leave our army?
translations.idiomatic: They said: "The court wishes to make peace with the remnant Jin — where does that leave our army?

sentences.zh: 」丙遣李全、季先拒之，不止，事甚危。

translations.literal: Bing sent Li Quan and Ji Xian to resist them, but they did not stop; the situation was extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Bing sent Li Quan and Ji Xian to resist them, but they would not stop; the situation was extremely perilous.

sentences.zh: 涉時在寶應，上書曰：「降附踵至，而金乃請和，此正用高澄間侯景遺策，恐山東之禍必移於兩淮。

translations.literal: At the time She was at Baoying and submitted a memorial saying: "Surrenderers arrive one after another, yet the Jin now seek peace — this is precisely the stratagem Gao Cheng used to sow discord with Hou Jing; I fear the disaster of Shandong will surely shift to the two Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jia She was at Baoying and submitted a memorial to the throne: "Defectors are arriving in an endless stream, yet the Jin now sue for peace — this is precisely the legacy stratagem of Gao Cheng driving a wedge against Hou Jing. I fear the calamity of Shandong will inevitably shift to the two Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 況金人所乏惟財與糧，若舉數年歲幣還之，是以肉㗖餒虎，㗖盡將反噬。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the Jin lack is only wealth and grain; if we return to them the annual tribute of several years, it is feeding meat to a starving tiger — once it finishes eating, it will turn and bite.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Jin lack nothing but wealth and grain. If we return to them several years' worth of annual tribute, it is feeding meat to a starving tiger — once it has eaten its fill, it will turn and bite.

sentences.zh: 至若忠義之人源源而來，不立定額，自為一軍，處之北岸，則安能以有限之財應無窮之須？

translations.literal: As for the loyal and righteous who come in an endless stream, if we do not establish fixed quotas and let them form their own army stationed on the north bank, how can limited resources meet infinite demands?
translations.idiomatic: As for the loyal and righteous who keep arriving in a steady stream, if we do not set fixed quotas and instead let them form their own army on the north bank, how can finite resources satisfy endless needs?

sentences.zh: 饑則噬人，飽則用命，其勢然也。

translations.literal: When hungry they devour men; when full they fight with zeal — such is the nature of the situation."
translations.idiomatic: When hungry they prey on men; when fed they fight with zeal — such is the nature of the situation."

sentences.zh: 」授淮東提點刑獄兼楚州節制本路京東忠義人兵。

translations.literal: He was appointed judicial intendant of Huaidong, concurrently charged with directing the loyal and righteous troops from Shandong in this circuit at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial intendant of Huaidong, concurrently charged with commanding the Shandong loyal and righteous forces of the circuit at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 涉亟遣傅翼諭珪等逆順禍福，自以輕車抵山陽，德廣等郊迎，伏地請死，誓以自新。

translations.literal: She urgently sent Fu Yi to explain to Gui and the others the fortunes and misfortunes of rebellion and loyalty; he himself took a light carriage to Shanyang; Deguang and the others welcomed him in the suburbs, prostrated themselves begging to die, and vowed to reform.
translations.idiomatic: She urgently dispatched Fu Yi to explain to Shi Gui and the others the consequences of rebellion versus loyalty, then personally took a light carriage to Shanyang. Yang Deguang and the others welcomed him in the suburbs, prostrated themselves begging for death, and vowed to reform.

sentences.zh: 金太子及僕散萬忠、盧國瑞等數十萬大入，且以計誘珪等。

translations.literal: The Jin crown prince together with Pusan Wanzong, Lu Guorui, and others invaded in force with hundreds of thousands of men, and also used stratagems to entice Gui and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin crown prince together with Pusan Wanzong, Lu Guorui, and others invaded with an army of hundreds of thousands, and also employed stratagems to entice Shi Gui and his followers.

sentences.zh: 涉慮珪等為金用，亟遣陳孝忠向滁州，珪與夏全、時青向濠州，先、平、德廣趨滁、濠，李全、李福要其歸路，以傅翼監軍。

translations.literal: She feared Gui and the others would be used by the Jin, and urgently dispatched Chen Xiaozhong toward Chuzhou; Gui with Xia Quan and Shi Qing toward Haozhou; Xian, Ping, and Deguang rushed to Chuzhou and Haozhou; Li Quan and Li Fu blocked their return route, with Fu Yi overseeing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Gui and the others would be turned to Jin use, She urgently dispatched Chen Xiaozhong toward Chuzhou; Shi Gui with Xia Quan and Shi Qing toward Haozhou; Ji Xian, Ge Ping, and Yang Deguang toward Chuzhou and Haozhou; Li Quan and Li Fu blocked their line of retreat, with Fu Yi supervising the army.

sentences.zh: 數日，孝忠捷至，珪屢破金人，遂與先及李全趨安豐。

translations.literal: Within days Xiaozhong's victory report arrived; Gui repeatedly defeated the Jin, then together with Xian and Li Quan advanced toward Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Chen Xiaozhong's victory report arrived. Shi Gui repeatedly defeated the Jin, then joined Ji Xian and Li Quan in advancing toward Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 時金人環百餘砦，攻具甫畢，珪等解其圍，李全挾僕散萬忠以歸，見《李全傳》。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin had surrounded more than a hundred stockades and had just finished preparing siege equipment; Gui and the others lifted the siege; Li Quan took Pusan Wanzong captive and returned — see the Biography of Li Quan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jin had encircled more than a hundred stockades and had just completed their siege equipment. Gui and the others broke the siege, and Li Quan took Pusan Wanzong captive and returned — see the Biography of Li Quan.

sentences.zh: 金人不敢窺淮東者六七年。

translations.literal: For six or seven years thereafter the Jin dared not cast eyes toward Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: For six or seven years thereafter the Jin dared not cast their gaze toward Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 南渡門之變，平、德廣等實預，涉既受降，置弗問。

translations.literal: In the incident at Nandu Gate, Ping and Deguang and others had actually participated; after She accepted their surrender, he set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ping and Yang Deguang and others had actually taken part in the Nandu Gate incident. After She accepted their surrender, he set the matter aside without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 平等尚懷異志，涉密使先以計殺之，而先之勢亦孤。

translations.literal: Ping and the others still harbored rebellious intent; She secretly had Xian devise a plan to kill them, and Xian's power thereafter stood alone.
translations.idiomatic: Ping and the others still harbored rebellious intent. She secretly had Ji Xian devise a plan to kill them, and Ji Xian's power thereafter stood alone.

sentences.zh: 忠義諸軍在漣水、山陽者既眾，涉慮其思亂，因滁、濠之役，分珪、孝忠、夏全為兩屯，李全軍為五砦，又用陝西義勇法涅其手，合諸軍汰者三萬有奇，涅者不滿六萬人，正軍常屯七萬餘，使主勝客，朝廷歲省費十三四。

translations.literal: The loyal and righteous armies at Lianshui and Shanyang had grown numerous; She feared they would turn to rebellion; using the Chuzhou and Haozhou campaign as pretext, he split Gui, Xiaozhong, and Xia Quan into two encampments and Li Quan's army into five stockades; he also adopted the Shaanxi volunteer method of tattooing their hands; after consolidating the armies and weeding out the unfit, more than thirty thousand were dismissed; those tattooed numbered fewer than sixty thousand, while regular troops normally stationed totaled over seventy thousand — making the host prevail over the guest, the court saved thirty or forty percent in annual expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and righteous armies at Lianshui and Shanyang had grown very large, and She feared they would turn to rebellion. Using the Chuzhou and Haozhou campaign as pretext, he split Shi Gui, Chen Xiaozhong, and Xia Quan into two encampments and Li Quan's army into five stockades. He also adopted the Shaanxi volunteer practice of tattooing their hands. After consolidating the armies and weeding out the unfit, more than thirty thousand were dismissed; those tattooed numbered fewer than sixty thousand, while regular troops in permanent garrison totaled over seventy thousand — making the host prevail over the guest, so the court saved thirty or forty percent in annual expenses.

sentences.zh: 涉又遣李全以萬人取海州，復取密、濰。

translations.literal: She also sent Li Quan with ten thousand men to take Haizhou, then recovered Mi and Wei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: She also sent Li Quan with ten thousand men to take Haizhou, then recovered Mi and Wei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 王琳以寧海州歸，遂收登、萊二州。

translations.literal: Wang Lin surrendered Ninghai Prefecture, and they then recovered Deng and Lai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin surrendered Ninghai Prefecture, and they then recovered Deng and Lai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 青州守張林以濱、棣、淄州降，又取濟、沂等州。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin, defender of Qingzhou, surrendered Bin, Di, and Zi prefectures, and they also took Ji, Yi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin, defender of Qingzhou, surrendered Bin, Di, and Zi prefectures, and they also took Ji, Yi, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 自是恩、博、景、德至邢、洺十餘州相繼請降。

translations.literal: From then on more than ten prefectures from En, Bo, Jing, and De to Xing and Ming successively requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: From then on more than ten prefectures from En, Bo, Jing, and De to Xing and Ming successively offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 涉傳檄中原：「以地來歸及反戈自效者，朝廷裂地封爵無所吝。

translations.literal: She issued a proclamation to the Central Plains: "Those who come over with territory and those who turn their swords in service — the court will divide lands and bestow titles without stint.
translations.idiomatic: She issued a proclamation to the Central Plains: "Those who submit with territory and those who turn their swords in loyal service — the court will divide lands and bestow titles without stint.

sentences.zh: 」仍厲諸將，圖未下州郡。

translations.literal: She also urged the generals to plan for prefectures and districts not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: She also urged the generals to target prefectures and districts not yet taken.

sentences.zh: 擢太府少卿、制置副使兼京東、河北節制。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Palace Treasury, vice commissioner for administration, concurrently directing affairs in Jingdong and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Palace Treasury and vice commissioner for administration, concurrently directing affairs in Jingdong and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 金十餘萬眾犯黃州，淮西帥趙善湘請援於朝，涉遣李全等赴之，翟朝宗等為後繼。

translations.literal: The Jin invaded Huangzhou with more than a hundred thousand men; Zhao Shanxiang, commander of Huai West, requested aid from court; She dispatched Li Quan and others, with Zhai Chaozong and others as reserve.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin invaded Huangzhou with more than a hundred thousand men. Zhao Shanxiang, commander of Huai West, requested aid from the court. She dispatched Li Quan and others, with Zhai Chaozong and others as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 丞相史彌遠擬升全留後，涉曰：「始全貧窶無聊，能輕財與眾同甘苦，故下樂為之用。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan proposed promoting Quan to acting military commissioner; She said: "At first Quan was destitute and desperate; he could lightly spend his own wealth to share hardship with the men, so his followers gladly served him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan proposed promoting Li Quan to acting military commissioner. She said: "At first Quan was destitute and desperate; he could freely spend his own wealth to share hardship with his men, so his followers gladly served him.

sentences.zh: 逮為主帥，所為反是，積怨既多，眾皆不平。

translations.literal: Once he became commander, his conduct was the opposite; resentment had accumulated and the men were all discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became commander, his conduct was the opposite. Resentment had accumulated and his men were all discontent.

sentences.zh: 近棄西城，免死為幸，若無故升遷以驕其誌，非全之福，亦豈國家之福。

translations.literal: Recently he abandoned Xicheng — escaping death was luck enough; if he is promoted without cause and his arrogance is fed, that is not Quan's blessing, nor is it the state's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Recently he abandoned Xicheng — escaping with his life was fortune enough. If he is promoted without cause and his arrogance is fed, that is not Quan's blessing, nor is it the state's blessing.

sentences.zh: 曷若待事定，與諸將同升可也。

translations.literal: Would it not be better to wait until matters are settled and promote him together with the other generals?"
translations.idiomatic: Would it not be better to wait until matters are settled and promote him together with the other generals?"

sentences.zh: 」金人破黃陷蘄，安慶甚危，全馳至，遂定。

translations.literal: The Jin broke Huang and captured Qi; Anqing was in grave danger; Quan galloped there and stabilized the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin broke through at Huang and captured Qi. Anqing was in grave danger, but Quan galloped there and stabilized the situation.

sentences.zh: 全至久長鎮，與京湖制置使趙方二子范、葵遇，掎角連戰俱勝，遣彭義斌等進至下灣渡，盡掩金人於淮。

translations.literal: Quan reached Jiuchang garrison and met Zhao Fang's sons Fan and Kui; fighting in pincer formation they won successive battles, and dispatched Peng Yibin and others to advance to Xiawan Ford, cutting off all Jin forces south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Quan reached Jiuchang garrison and joined Zhao Fang's sons Fan and Kui. Fighting in pincer formation they won successive battles, and dispatched Peng Yibin and others to advance to Xiawan Ford, cutting off all Jin forces south of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 遷權吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 金人再犯淮西。

translations.literal: The Jin again invaded Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin again invaded Huai West.

sentences.zh: 先是，蘄州受圍，徐暉往援，乃鼓眾宵遁，金乘間登城，一郡為血，前帥不敢問。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qizhou was besieged, Xu Hui went to its relief but instead roused his troops to flee by night; the Jin seized the opportunity to scale the walls; the whole prefecture ran with blood; the previous commander dared not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qizhou was besieged, Xu Hui went to its relief but instead roused his troops to flee by night. The Jin seized the opportunity to scale the walls; the whole prefecture ran with blood. The previous commander dared not investigate.

sentences.zh: 涉斬暉以徇，諸將畏懼，無不用命，淮西之勢大振。

translations.literal: She executed Hui as a warning; the generals feared and all obeyed without question; Huai West's position greatly strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: She executed Xu Hui as a warning. The generals were awed and all obeyed without question; Huai West's position was greatly strengthened.

sentences.zh: 初，翟朝宗得玉璽獻諸朝，至是趙拱還，又得玉印，文與璽同而加大。

translations.literal: Early on, Zhai Chaozong obtained a jade seal and presented it to court; now Zhao Gong returned and obtained a jade stamp; the inscription matched the seal but was larger.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhai Chaozong had obtained a jade seal and presented it to the court. Now Zhao Gong returned and obtained a jade stamp; its inscription matched the seal but was larger.

sentences.zh: 朝廷喜璧之歸，行慶賞。

translations.literal: The court rejoiced at the return of the jade treasure and conducted celebratory rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejoiced at the return of the jade treasure and conducted celebratory rewards.

sentences.zh: 涉遺書彌遠謂：「天意隱而難明，人事切而易見，當思今日人事尚未有可答天意者。

translations.literal: She sent Shi Miyuan a letter saying: "Heaven's intent is hidden and hard to discern; human affairs are pressing and easy to see; one should consider that today's human affairs have not yet reached a point that could answer Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: She sent Shi Miyuan a letter saying: "Heaven's intent is hidden and hard to discern, while human affairs are pressing and easy to see. One should consider that today's human affairs have not yet reached a point that could answer Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 昔之患不過亡金，今之患又有山東忠義與北邊，宜亟圖之。

translations.literal: Formerly the worry was nothing beyond losing the Jin; now there are also the Shandong loyalists and the northern frontier — these should be urgently addressed."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the worry was nothing beyond losing the Jin. Now there are also the Shandong loyalists and the northern frontier — these should be urgently addressed."

sentences.zh: 」彌遠不懌，李全卒以璽賞為節度使。

translations.literal: Miyuan was displeased; Li Quan was ultimately rewarded with the seal and appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan was displeased. Li Quan was ultimately rewarded with the seal and appointed military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 涉又言：「盜賊血氣正盛，官職過分，將有後憂。

translations.literal: She also said: "These bandits' fighting spirit is at its peak; excessive official rank will bring trouble later.
translations.idiomatic: She also said: "These bandits' fighting spirit is at its peak. Excessive official rank will bring trouble later.

sentences.zh: 」彌遠不以為然。

translations.literal: Miyuan did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan did not agree.

sentences.zh: 涉曰：「朝廷但知官爵可以得其心，寧知驕則將至於不可勸邪？」

translations.literal: She said: "The court thinks only that rank and title can win their hearts — does it not know that once pride sets in they will become beyond persuasion?"
translations.idiomatic: She said: "The court thinks only that rank and title can win their hearts — does it not know that once pride sets in they will become beyond persuasion?"

sentences.zh: 涉時已疾，力辭事任。

translations.literal: She was already ill and strenuously declined his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was already ill and strenuously declined his duties.

sentences.zh: 值金人大入，強起視事。

translations.literal: When the Jin invaded on a large scale, he forced himself to rise and attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded on a large scale, he forced himself to rise and attend to affairs.

sentences.zh: 金將時全、合連、孛術魯答哥率細軍及眾軍三道渡淮，涉以合連善戰，乃命張惠當之。

translations.literal: Jin generals Shi Quan, Helian, and Bieshulu Dage led elite troops and main forces in three columns across the Huai; She, knowing Helian was skilled in battle, ordered Zhang Hui to confront him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin generals Shi Quan, Helian, and Bieshulu Dage led elite troops and main forces in three columns across the Huai. She, knowing Helian was skilled in battle, ordered Zhang Hui to confront him.

sentences.zh: 惠，金驍將，所謂「賽張飛」者，既歸宋，金人殺其妻，所部花帽軍，有紀律，它軍不及也。

translations.literal: Hui was a fierce Jin general, known as "rival to Zhang Fei"; after defecting to Song, the Jin killed his wife; his Flower-Cap Army was disciplined beyond other troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a fierce Jin general known as "Rival to Zhang Fei." After defecting to Song, the Jin killed his wife. His Flower-Cap Army was disciplined beyond any other force.

sentences.zh: 惠率諸軍出戰，自辰至酉，金人大敗，答哥溺死，陷失太半，細軍喪者幾二千。

translations.literal: Hui led the armies out to battle; from the hour of Chen to You the Jin suffered great defeat; Dage drowned, over half were lost, and nearly two thousand elite troops perished.
translations.idiomatic: Hui led the armies out to battle. From the hour of Chen to You the Jin suffered a crushing defeat. Dage drowned, over half the force was lost, and nearly two thousand elite troops perished.

sentences.zh: 涉既病，乃以所獲京、河版籍及金銀牌銅印之屬上於朝。

translations.literal: When She was already ill, he submitted to court the registers of Jing and He and items such as gold and silver tally-slips and bronze seals that had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: When She was already ill, he submitted to the court the registers of Jing and He and items such as gold and silver tally-slips and bronze seals that had been captured.

sentences.zh: 卒，超贈龍圖閣學士、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously advanced to Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously advanced to Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 涉父偉，嘗守開江，貽書丞相趙雄，極論武興守吳挺之橫，它日陛對，又乞裁抑郭棣、郭杲兵權，孝宗嘉納，後反為所擠以沒。

translations.literal: She's father Wei had once served as defender of Kaijiang; he sent Chief Councilor Zhao Xiong a letter vehemently denouncing Wu Ting's tyranny as defender of Wuxing; on another day at court audience he also requested curbing the military authority of Guo Di and Guo Gao; Xiaozong approved, but later he was squeezed out by them and died in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: She's father Wei had once served as defender of Kaijiang. He sent Chief Councilor Zhao Xiong a letter vehemently denouncing Wu Ting's tyranny as defender of Wuxing; on another day at court audience he also requested curbing the military authority of Guo Di and Guo Gao. Xiaozong approved, but later he was squeezed out by them and died in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 涉弱冠直父冤，不避寒暑，泣訴十年，至伏書闕下。

translations.literal: In his early twenties She sought justice for his father's wrong; unmindful of heat and cold, he wept and appealed for ten years, finally prostrating himself with a petition below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties She sought justice for his father's wrong. Unmindful of heat and cold, he wept and appealed for ten years, finally prostrating himself with a petition below the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 子：似道，有傳。

translations.literal: Son: Sidao — see separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Sidao — see separate biography.

sentences.zh: 扈再興

translations.literal: Hu Zaixing
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zaixing

sentences.zh: 扈再興，字叔起，淮人也。

translations.literal: Hu Zaixing, courtesy name Shuji, was a native of the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zaixing, styled Shuji, came from the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 有膂力，善機變。

translations.literal: He possessed great physical strength and was skilled at improvisation.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed great physical strength and was skilled at improvisation.

sentences.zh: 每戰，被髮肉袒徒跣，揮雙刃奮呼入陣，人馬辟易。

translations.literal: In every battle he let his hair hang loose, bared his torso, and fought barefoot, wielding twin blades with fierce cries as he charged into the enemy ranks; men and horses gave way before him.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he let his hair hang loose, bared his torso, and fought barefoot, wielding twin blades with fierce cries as he charged into the enemy ranks. Men and horses gave way before him.

sentences.zh: 金人犯襄陽、棗陽，京西制置使趙方檄再興等禦之。

translations.literal: When the Jin invaded Xiangyang and Zaoyang, Jingxi commissioner Zhao Fang ordered Zaixing and others to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded Xiangyang and Zaoyang, Jingxi commissioner for administration Zhao Fang ordered Zaixing and others to resist.

sentences.zh: 金人來自團山，勢如風雨。

translations.literal: The Jin came from Tuan Mountain with the force of a windstorm.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin came from Tuan Mountain with the force of a windstorm.

sentences.zh: 再興同孟宗政、陳祥分三陳，設伏以待。

translations.literal: Zaixing together with Meng Zongzheng and Chen Xiang divided into three formations and laid ambushes in wait.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing together with Meng Zongzheng and Chen Xiang divided into three formations and laid ambushes in wait.

sentences.zh: 既至，再興中出一陳，復卻，金人逐之，宗政與祥合左右兩翼掩擊之，金人三面受敵，大敗，血肉枕藉山谷間。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Zaixing led the center formation out, then feigned retreat; the Jin pursued; Zongzheng and Xiang joined the left and right wings in a flanking attack; the Jin faced enemies on three sides and were routed; corpses piled thick in the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin arrived, Zaixing led the center formation out, then feigned retreat. The Jin pursued, and Zongzheng and Xiang joined the left and right wings in a flanking attack. The Jin faced enemies on three sides and were routed; corpses piled thick in the valleys.

sentences.zh: 授神勁統制。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of the Shenjin Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of the Shenjin Army.

sentences.zh: 又犯棗陽，再興率師赴援，金人聞風夜潰。

translations.literal: They again invaded Zaoyang; Zaixing led troops to the relief; the Jin, hearing of his approach, fled in the night.
translations.idiomatic: They again invaded Zaoyang. Zaixing led troops to the relief, and the Jin, hearing of his approach, fled in the night.

sentences.zh: 既而益兵數萬復圍城，相持九十日。

translations.literal: Soon after they added tens of thousands of troops and again besieged the city; the stalemate lasted ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after they added tens of thousands of troops and again besieged the city. The stalemate lasted ninety days.

sentences.zh: 再興夜以鐵蒺藜密布地，黎明佯遁，金人馳中蒺藜者十踣七八。

translations.literal: Zaixing scattered caltrops densely on the ground by night; at dawn he feigned retreat; Jin cavalry charging in — seven or eight of ten fell to the caltrops.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing scattered caltrops densely on the ground by night. At dawn he feigned retreat, and of the Jin cavalry that charged in, seven or eight of ten fell to the caltrops.

sentences.zh: 敵卻走，追至十五里岡。

translations.literal: The enemy turned and fled; he pursued them to Fifteen-Li Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy turned and fled, and he pursued them to Fifteen-Li Ridge.

sentences.zh: 已而金兵攻城東隅，薄南門北角，再興與宗政、劉世興各當一面，大戰數十合，大敗金兵。

translations.literal: Later Jin troops attacked the southeast corner of the city, pressing the north corner of the south gate; Zaixing with Zongzheng and Liu Shixing each held one face; after dozens of major clashes they routed the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jin troops attacked the southeast corner of the city, pressing the north corner of the south gate. Zaixing with Zongzheng and Liu Shixing each held one sector. After dozens of major clashes they routed the Jin.

sentences.zh: 金帥完顏訛可擁步騎數萬傅城，再興與宗政縱之涉濠，半渡擊之；

translations.literal: Jin commander Wanyan Eke led tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to the city walls; Zaixing and Zongzheng let them cross the moat and struck when half had crossed;
translations.idiomatic: Jin commander Wanyan Eke led tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to the city walls. Zaixing and Zongzheng let them cross the moat and struck when half had crossed;

sentences.zh: 又令守壩者佯走，金人爭壩，急擊之，多墮水中。

translations.literal: He also had the dam defenders feign flight; the Jin scrambled for the dam and he struck swiftly — many plunged into the water.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the dam defenders feign flight. The Jin scrambled for the dam and he struck swiftly — many plunged into the water.

sentences.zh: 金人創對樓、鵝車、革洞，決濠水，運土石填城下。

translations.literal: The Jin built siege towers, goose carts, and leather tunnels, diverted the moat water, and hauled earth and stone to fill beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin built siege towers, goose carts, and leather tunnels, diverted the moat water, and hauled earth and stone to fill beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 再興募死士著鐵面具，披氈，列陳以待之。

translations.literal: Zaixing recruited dare-to-die troops in iron masks wearing felt cloaks, arrayed in formation to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing recruited dare-to-die troops in iron masks wearing felt cloaks, arrayed in formation to await them.

sentences.zh: 金人計無所施而去，棄旗甲輜重滿野。

translations.literal: The Jin, finding no plan avail, withdrew, abandoning banners, armor, and supplies that covered the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin, finding no stratagem avail, withdrew, abandoning banners, armor, and supplies that covered the fields.

sentences.zh: 大戰於范家莊，金人敗，追之至泊湖，禽其巡檢亢師禮酒、都監納蘭福昌，降其壯丁，獲牛馬甚眾。

translations.literal: A great battle at Fan Family Village — the Jin were defeated; pursuit reached Bo Lake; they captured patrol inspector Kang Shili and superintendent Nalan Fuchang, accepted the surrender of able-bodied men, and seized many oxen and horses.
translations.idiomatic: At Fan Family Village a great battle was fought and the Jin were defeated. Pursuit reached Bo Lake; they captured patrol inspector Kang Shili and superintendent Nalan Fuchang, accepted the surrender of able-bodied men, and seized many oxen and horses.

sentences.zh: 自是與宗政、世興無日不戰。

translations.literal: From then on he battled with Zongzheng and Shixing without a day of rest.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he battled with Zongzheng and Shixing without a day of rest.

sentences.zh: 再興又破順昌縣，奪甲馬三千，破淅川鎮，殺金人三百，追至馬磴砦，焚其城柵。

translations.literal: Zaixing also broke Shunchang County, seizing three thousand sets of armor and horses; broke Xichuan garrison, killing three hundred Jin; pursued to Madeng Stockade and burned its fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing also broke Shunchang County, seizing three thousand sets of armor and horses. He broke Xichuan garrison, killing three hundred Jin, pursued to Madeng Stockade, and burned its fortifications.

sentences.zh: 又敗其護駕騎軍於瀼河。

translations.literal: He again defeated their imperial escort cavalry at the Rang River.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated their imperial escort cavalry at the Rang River.

sentences.zh: 入鄧州，破高頭，敗其步軍五千、騎軍五百，焚其積聚。

translations.literal: Entering Dengzhou, he broke Gaotou, defeated five thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry, and burned their stores.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Dengzhou, he broke Gaotou, defeated five thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry, and burned their stores.

sentences.zh: 遂營於高頭，進攻唐州，至三家河，金騎軍二千、步軍七千出城迎戰，又敗之，死者十七八，追及城下。

translations.literal: He then encamped at Gaotou and advanced on Tangzhou to Sanjia River; two thousand Jin cavalry and seven thousand infantry came out to fight; he defeated them again — seventy or eighty percent were killed — and pursued to the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: He then encamped at Gaotou and advanced on Tangzhou to Sanjia River. Two thousand Jin cavalry and seven thousand infantry came out to fight; he defeated them again — seventy or eighty percent were killed — and pursued to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 金將從義者收殘騎三百奔城，再興據門拒戰，斬從義。

translations.literal: A Jin officer named Congyi gathered three hundred remnant cavalry and rushed the gate; Zaixing held the gate and fought, beheading Congyi.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin officer named Congyi gathered three hundred remnant cavalry and rushed the gate. Zaixing held the gate and fought, beheading Congyi.

sentences.zh: 遂圍唐州，分兵焚蕩州境，截其歸路，砦於久長，嚴陳以待之。

translations.literal: He then besieged Tangzhou, sent detachments to burn and ravage the prefecture, cut off retreat routes, and encamped at Jiuchang in strict formation awaiting them.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Tangzhou, sent detachments to burn and ravage the prefecture, cut off retreat routes, and encamped at Jiuchang in strict formation awaiting them.

sentences.zh: 搜剿殘兵，獲其副統軍廣威將軍衲撻達。

translations.literal: In mopping up remnant troops he captured deputy commander, General of Expanding Might Nadatu.
translations.idiomatic: In mopping up remnant troops he captured deputy commander, General of Expanding Might Nadatu.

sentences.zh: 金兵殲，乃斂髑髏立人頭堠。

translations.literal: When the Jin forces were annihilated, he gathered skulls and erected a mound of heads.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin forces were annihilated, he gathered skulls and erected a mound of heads.

sentences.zh: 尋以病卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子世達，亦以名將稱，官至都統制。

translations.literal: His son Shida was also renowned as a fine general, rising to commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shida was also renowned as a fine general, rising to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 孟宗政

translations.literal: Meng Zongzheng
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zongzheng

sentences.zh: 孟宗政，字德夫，絳州人。

translations.literal: Meng Zongzheng, courtesy name Defu, was a native of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zongzheng, styled Defu, came from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父林，從岳飛至隨州，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Lin followed Yue Fei to Suizhou and settled the family there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lin followed Yue Fei to Suizhou and settled the family there.

sentences.zh: 宗政自幼豪偉，有膽略，常出沒疆場間。

translations.literal: Zongzheng was bold and imposing from youth, possessed of courage and strategy, and often ranged the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng was bold and imposing from youth, possessed of courage and strategy, and often ranged the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年，金將完顏董犯襄、郢，宗政率義士據險遊擊，奪其輜重。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaixi, Jin general Wanyan Dong invaded Xiang and Ying; Zongzheng led volunteers to strike from ambush in rugged terrain, seizing their baggage.
translations.idiomatic: In 1206, the second year of Kaixi, Jin general Wanyan Dong invaded Xiang and Ying. Zongzheng led volunteers to strike from ambush in rugged terrain, seizing their baggage.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使吳獵奇之，補承節郎、棗陽令。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Wu Lie admired him and appointed him Gentlemen for Upholding Integrity and magistrate of Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Wu Lie admired him and appointed him Gentlemen for Upholding Integrity and magistrate of Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 京西路分趙方、吳柔勝皆薦其才，轉秉義郎、京西鈐轄，駐劄襄陽。

translations.literal: Jingxi circuit commissioners Zhao Fang and Wu Rousheng both recommended his talent; he was transferred to Gentleman for Maintaining Righteousness and Jingxi chief controller, stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxi circuit commissioners Zhao Fang and Wu Rousheng both recommended his talent. He was transferred to Gentleman for Maintaining Righteousness and Jingxi chief controller, stationed at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年，金人犯襄陽、棗陽，方檄宗政節制神勁、報捷、忠義三軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiading the Jin invaded Xiangyang and Zaoyang; Fang ordered Zongzheng to command the Shenjin, Baojie, and Loyal and Righteous armies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1217, the tenth year of Jiading, the Jin invaded Xiangyang and Zaoyang. Zhao Fang ordered Zongzheng to command the Shenjin, Baojie, and Loyal and Righteous armies.

sentences.zh: 宗政與統製扈再興、陳祥分為三軍，設伏三所，蹀血以戰，金兵敗走。

translations.literal: Zongzheng with commanders Hu Zaixing and Chen Xiang divided into three armies, setting three ambushes, fighting through blood-soaked ground until the Jin fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng with commanders Hu Zaixing and Chen Xiang divided into three armies, setting three ambushes. They fought through blood-soaked ground until the Jin fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 尋報棗陽圍急，宗政午發峴首，遲明抵棗陽，馳突如神。

translations.literal: Soon word came that Zaoyang's siege was critical; Zongzheng departed Xianshou at noon and reached Zaoyang by daybreak, charging like a god.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Zaoyang's siege was critical. Zongzheng departed Xianshou at noon and reached Zaoyang by daybreak, charging like a god.

sentences.zh: 金人大駭，宵遁。

translations.literal: The Jin were greatly alarmed and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were greatly alarmed and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 方時移帥京西，聞捷大喜，差權棗陽軍。

translations.literal: Fang had just been transferred as Jingxi commander; hearing the victory he was overjoyed and appointed Zongzheng acting administrator of Zaoyang Military Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had just been transferred as Jingxi commander. Hearing of the victory he was overjoyed and appointed Zongzheng acting administrator of Zaoyang Military Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初眡事，一愛僕犯新令，立斬之，軍民股栗。

translations.literal: On first assuming office, a favored servant violated a new regulation and he immediately executed him; troops and civilians trembled with awe.
translations.idiomatic: On first assuming office, a favored servant violated a new regulation and he immediately executed him. Troops and civilians trembled with awe.

sentences.zh: 於是築隄積水，修治城堞，簡閱軍士。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built dikes to store water, repaired the battlements, and inspected the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he built dikes to store water, repaired the battlements, and inspected the troops.

sentences.zh: 十一年，金帥完顏賽不擁步騎圍城，宗政與再興合兵角敵，歷三月，大小七十餘戰，宗政身先士卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Jin commander Wanyan Saibuo led infantry and cavalry to besiege the city; Zongzheng and Zaixing combined forces to contend with the enemy; over three months they fought more than seventy battles large and small, with Zongzheng always leading from the front.
translations.idiomatic: In 1218, the eleventh year of Jiading, Jin commander Wanyan Saibuo led infantry and cavalry to besiege the city. Zongzheng and Zaixing combined forces to contend with the enemy. Over three months they fought more than seventy battles large and small, with Zongzheng always leading from the front.

sentences.zh: 金人戰輒敗，忿甚，周城開濠，四面控兵列濠外，飛鋒鏑，以鈴自警，鈴響則犬吠。

translations.literal: The Jin lost every battle and grew furious; they dug a moat around the city, posted troops on all sides beyond the moat, fired whistling arrows, used bells as alarms — when bells rang, dogs barked.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin lost every battle and grew furious. They dug a moat around the city, posted troops on all sides beyond the moat, fired whistling arrows, and used bells as alarms — when bells rang, dogs barked.

sentences.zh: 宗政厚募壯士，乘間突擊，金人不能支，盛兵薄城，宗政隨方力拒。

translations.literal: Zongzheng generously recruited bold men for opportune strikes; when the Jin could not hold, they massed troops against the walls and Zongzheng resisted wherever they pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng generously recruited bold men for opportune strikes. When the Jin could not hold, they massed troops against the walls and Zongzheng resisted wherever they pressed.

sentences.zh: 隨守許國援師至白水，鼓聲相聞。

translations.literal: Suizhou defender Xu Guo's relief force reached Baishui; the sound of drums could be heard between the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Suizhou defender Xu Guo's relief force reached Baishui; the sound of drums could be heard between the armies.

sentences.zh: 宗政率諸將出戰，金人奔潰。

translations.literal: Zongzheng led the generals out to battle and the Jin broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng led the generals out to battle and the Jin broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 賜金帶，轉武德郎。

translations.literal: He was granted a gold belt and transferred to Wude Lang.
translations.idiomatic: He was awarded a gold belt and promoted to the rank of Wude Lang.

sentences.zh: 十二年，金帥完顏訛可擁步騎傅城，宗政囊糠盛沙以覆樓棚，列甕瀦水以隄火，募砲手擊之，一砲輒殺數人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Jin commander Wanyan Eke led infantry and cavalry to press against the city walls; Zongzheng stuffed sacks with chaff filled with sand to cover the tower shelters, lined jars of stored water as a fire barrier, recruited artillerymen to strike them, and each shot killed several men.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Jin commander Wanyan Eke led infantry and cavalry to the foot of the walls. Zongzheng had sacks of chaff filled with sand to shield the tower platforms, lined jars of water as a firebreak, and recruited artillery crews; a single shot would kill several men.

sentences.zh: 金人選精騎二千，號弩子手，擁雲梯、天橋先登，又募鑿銀礦石工晝夜塪城，運茅葦直抵圜樓下，欲焚樓。

translations.literal: The Jin selected two thousand elite cavalry called crossbow handlers, brought scaling ladders and sky bridges to ascend first, also recruited miners who day and night undermined the walls, transported thatch and reeds straight to the foot of the round tower, intending to burn the tower.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin picked two thousand elite horsemen, called crossbow handlers, and sent them forward with scaling ladders and sky bridges. They also hired miners to undermine the walls day and night, hauled thatch and reeds right up to the round tower, and planned to burn it down.

sentences.zh: 宗政先毀樓，掘深坑，防地道；

translations.literal: Zongzheng first demolished the tower, dug deep pits, guarding against tunnels;
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng first tore down the tower and dug deep pits to guard against tunneling;

sentences.zh: 創戰棚，防城損；

translations.literal: created battle sheds, guarding against damage to the walls;
translations.idiomatic: built fighting platforms to protect the walls from damage;

sentences.zh: 穿穽才透，即施毒煙烈火，鼓韝以熏之。

translations.literal: as soon as a tunnel broke through, he applied poisonous smoke and fierce fire, blowing bellows to smoke them out.
translations.idiomatic: the moment a tunnel broke through, he poured in poisonous smoke and raging fire and worked bellows to fumigate the enemy.

sentences.zh: 金人窒以濕氈，析路以刳士，城頹樓陷。

translations.literal: The Jin blocked with wet felt, cleared paths and dug out earth; the wall collapsed and the tower fell in.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin blocked the smoke with wet felt, cleared routes, and dug away the earth; the wall gave way and the tower collapsed.

sentences.zh: 宗政撤樓益薪，架火山以絕其路，列勇士，以長槍勁弩備其衝。

translations.literal: Zongzheng removed the tower and piled fuel, set up a fire wall to cut off their path, arrayed brave warriors, and with long spears and powerful crossbows prepared against their assault.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng cleared the tower and piled fuel, built a fire barrier to block their advance, and lined up brave fighters with long spears and heavy crossbows to meet the assault.

sentences.zh: 距樓陷所數丈築偃月城，袤百餘尺，翼傅正城，深坑倍仞，躬督役，五日成。

translations.literal: Several zhang from where the tower had fallen he built a crescent moon fort over a hundred chi in length, flanking the main wall, with pits twice the depth of ren; he personally supervised the work, and it was completed in five days.
