translations.idiomatic: A few zhang from where the tower had collapsed, he built a crescent-shaped redoubt over a hundred chi long, flanking the main wall, with pits twice a ren deep. He personally oversaw the labor, and it was finished in five days.

sentences.zh: 金人摘強兵披厚鎧、氈衫、鐵面而前，又濕氈濡革蒙火山，覆以冰雪，擁雲梯徑抵西北圜樓登城。

translations.literal: The Jin picked strong troops wearing thick armor, felt coats, and iron face masks to advance; again they covered the fire wall with wet felt and soaked leather, overlaying it with ice and snow, and brought scaling ladders straight to the northwest round tower to mount the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent picked troops forward in thick armor, felt jackets, and iron face guards. They again smothered the fire barrier with wet felt and soaked hides, piled ice and snow on top, and pushed scaling ladders straight to the northwest round tower to climb the wall.

sentences.zh: 城中軍以長戈舂其喉，殺之；

translations.literal: The city's troops used long halberds to thrust at their throats and killed them;
translations.idiomatic: The garrison thrust long halberds at their throats and killed them;

sentences.zh: 敢勇軍自下夾擊金兵，兵墜死燎焰。

translations.literal: the Dare-to-Be-Brave Army attacked the Jin troops from below on both sides; the soldiers fell and died in the flames.
translations.idiomatic: the Dare-to-Be-Brave Corps struck the Jin from below on both flanks, and men fell to their deaths in the blaze.

sentences.zh: 金將於後截其軍，拒馬揮刀迫前，自昕至昃，死傷踵接，梯橋盡燬。

translations.literal: A Jin general cut off their rear, pushed forward with caltrops and swinging blades; from morning to midday the dead and wounded followed one after another, and ladders and bridges were all burned.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin commander cut off their rear and pressed forward behind caltrops, blades swinging. From dawn to midday the dead and wounded came in an unbroken stream, and every ladder and bridge was burned.

sentences.zh: 金人連不得志，俄乘順風渡濠，飛脂革燒戰棚，宗政激將士血戰，凡十五陣，矢石交，金兵死者千餘，弩子手十七八，射其都統殪。

translations.literal: The Jin repeatedly failed; soon riding a favorable wind they crossed the moat, hurled greased leather to burn the battle sheds; Zongzheng roused his officers and men to fight a bloody battle in fifteen formations; arrows and stones flew; over a thousand Jin soldiers died, only seventeen or eighteen of the crossbow handlers survived, and they shot dead their commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated again and again, the Jin soon rode a favorable wind across the moat and hurled greased hides to set the fighting platforms ablaze. Zongzheng roused his officers and men to a bloody fight through fifteen engagements. Arrows and stones flew back and forth; more than a thousand Jin soldiers were killed, only seventeen or eighteen crossbow handlers remained, and they shot their commander dead.

sentences.zh: 天反風，金人愈忿，炮愈急。

translations.literal: The wind shifted; the Jin grew even angrier and their artillery fire grew even fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The wind turned against them; the Jin grew angrier still, and their bombardment grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 會王大任領銳卒一千冒重圍轉鬥入城，內外合勢，士氣大振，賈勇入金營，自晡至三更，金人橫屍遍地，奪其銅印十有六，訛可棄帳走，獲輜重牛馬萬計。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Daren led a thousand crack troops, broke through the heavy encirclement fighting their way into the city; inner and outer forces combined, morale soared greatly; emboldened they entered the Jin camp; from the afternoon watch until the third watch of night Jin corpses lay strewn across the ground; they seized sixteen bronze seals; Eke abandoned his tent and fled; baggage, cattle and horses captured numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wang Daren led a thousand elite troops, broke through the tight encirclement, and fought his way into the city. Inner and outer forces joined, and morale surged. Emboldened, they charged into the Jin camp. From midafternoon until the third watch of night, Jin corpses covered the ground. They captured sixteen bronze seals. Eke abandoned his headquarters and fled. Baggage, cattle, and horses taken numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 捷至，朝廷方錄前戰守功，升武功大夫兼閤門宣贊舍人，重賜金帶。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the court was just then recording previous merits in battle and defense; he was promoted to Military Meritorious Grand Master concurrently Gate Herald and Praise Master, and again granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory arrived, the court was already tallying earlier merits in defense and attack. He was promoted to Military Meritorious Grand Master and concurrently appointed Gate Herald and Praise Master, and was again awarded a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 制置司以湖陽縣迫境金兵，檄宗政圖之。

translations.literal: The military commissionerate, because Huyang County bordered Jin troops, issued orders to Zongzheng to deal with them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huyang County lay on the Jin border, the military commissionerate ordered Zongzheng to take action.

sentences.zh: 宗政一鼓而拔，燔燒積聚，夷蕩營砦，俘掠以歸。

translations.literal: Zongzheng took it at the first assault, burned their stores, razed their camps and fortifications, and returned with captives and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng captured the place at the first rush, burned their stockpiles, leveled their camps and fortifications, and returned with prisoners and booty.

sentences.zh: 金人自是不敢窺襄、漢、棗陽。

translations.literal: From then on the Jin no longer dared cast covetous eyes on Xiang, Han, and Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Jin no longer dared threaten Xiang, Han, or Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 許國移金陵，宗政代為荊鄂都統制，仍知棗陽。

translations.literal: Xu Guo was transferred to Jinling; Zongzheng replaced him as overall commander of Jing-E, and still served as prefect of Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Guo was transferred to Jinling, Zongzheng succeeded him as overall commander of Jing-E while continuing as prefect of Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 宗政以迫濠而陳，乃於西北濠外瀦水為濘以限騎。

translations.literal: Zongzheng, because the army was drawn up close to the moat, dammed water outside the northwest moat to create muddy ground to limit cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Because his forces were deployed too close to the moat, Zongzheng dammed water outside the northwest ditch to create muddy ground that would check cavalry.

sentences.zh: 中原遺民來歸者以萬數。

translations.literal: Refugees from the Central Plains who came to submit numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from the Central Plains who came over to the Song numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 宗政發廩贍之，為給田、創屋與居，籍其勇壯號「忠順軍」，俾出沒唐、鄧間，威振境外。

translations.literal: Zongzheng distributed grain from the granaries to sustain them, allotted fields and built houses for them to dwell in, registered their brave and strong as the Loyal and Obedient Army, had them operate between Tang and Deng, and his renown shook lands beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng opened the granaries to feed them, allotted fields, built houses for them to live in, and enrolled their stout fighters in a force called the Loyal and Obedient Army, which he sent raiding between Tang and Deng. His fame shook the country beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 金人呼為「孟爺爺」。

translations.literal: The Jin called him Grandfather Meng.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin called him "Grandfather Meng."

sentences.zh: 俄病疽卒。

translations.literal: Soon he sickened with a carbuncle and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill with a festering sore and died.

sentences.zh: 轉右武大夫、團練使、防禦使。

translations.literal: He was posthumously promoted to Right Military Grand Master, regimental training commissioner, and defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted to Right Military Grand Master, regimental training commissioner, and defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宗政於有功者怨必賞，有罪者親必罰。

translations.literal: Zongzheng always rewarded those who had merit even if he bore a grudge against them, and always punished those who were guilty even if they were close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzheng always rewarded men of merit even when he personally resented them, and always punished the guilty even when they were close to him.

sentences.zh: 好賢樂善，出於天性。

translations.literal: He loved the worthy and delighted in good deeds — this came from his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the worthy and took pleasure in doing good — traits that sprang from his nature.

sentences.zh: 未嘗學兵法，而暗與之合。

translations.literal: He had never studied military arts, yet his actions tacitly accorded with them.
translations.idiomatic: He had never studied the art of war, yet what he did tacitly matched its principles.

sentences.zh: 死之日，邊城為罷市慟哭。

translations.literal: On the day he died, the border cities closed their markets and wept in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his death, the frontier towns closed their markets and mourned him with weeping.

sentences.zh: 子：珙，有傳。

translations.literal: Son: Gong, who has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Gong, who has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 張威，字德遠，成州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, courtesy name Deyuan, was a native of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, styled Deyuan, came from Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 策選鋒軍騎兵也。

translations.literal: He was selected by examination for the vanguard army's cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen by examination for the vanguard army's cavalry.

sentences.zh: 軍中馬料多，匹馬給米五石，騎軍利其餘以自給。

translations.literal: In the army horse fodder allowances were generous; each horse was allotted five shi of rice, and the cavalry profited from the surplus for their own sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: Army fodder allowances were generous: each horse drew five shi of rice, and the horsemen pocketed the surplus to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 總領覈實裁抑，威逃去。

translations.literal: The commissioner-general verified accounts and cut back allowances; Wei fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the supply commissioner audited the accounts and cut the allowances, Wei deserted.

sentences.zh: 帥郭杲使其父招之歸，送隆慶府後軍效用。

translations.literal: Commander Guo Gao had his father summon him back and sent him to serve in the rear army of Longqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The commander Guo Gao had Wei's father bring him back and assigned him to the rear service corps of Longqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 威貧甚，賣藥自給。

translations.literal: Wei was extremely poor and sold medicine to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was desperately poor and sold medicine to get by.

sentences.zh: 或言其才勇，乃令戍邊。

translations.literal: Someone spoke of his talent and bravery, and he was then ordered to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When someone praised his talent and courage, he was ordered to the frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 開禧用兵，威與金人戰輒捷，屢以功補本軍將領。

translations.literal: During the Kaixi military campaign, Wei was invariably victorious in battles with the Jin and was repeatedly promoted within his army for his merits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaixi campaign, Wei won every clash with the Jin and was repeatedly promoted within his own army for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 吳曦既誅，遣將收復。

translations.literal: After Wu Xi was executed, the court dispatched generals to recover lost territory.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Xi was put to death, the court sent generals to recover lost ground.

sentences.zh: 李貴復西和州，威率眾先登，敗金人，戰於板橋，遂取西和，升統制。

translations.literal: Li Gui recovered Xihe Prefecture; Wei led his men to ascend first, defeated the Jin, fought at Banqiao, then took Xihe and was promoted to regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui retook Xihe Prefecture. Wei led his men up first, routed the Jin, fought at Banqiao, seized Xihe, and was promoted to regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 由是威名大振。

translations.literal: From this his martial renown greatly resounded.
translations.idiomatic: From that point his martial fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 天水縣當金人西入路，乃升縣為軍，命威為守，屢立奇功，擢充利州副都統制。

translations.literal: Tianshui County lay on the Jin route of advance from the west; the county was therefore elevated to a military prefecture and Wei was appointed its defender; he repeatedly performed outstanding feats and was promoted to deputy overall commander of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshui County stood on the Jin route of advance from the west, so the county was raised to a military prefecture and Wei was made its commander. He won repeated feats of distinction and was promoted to deputy overall commander of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，帶御器械。

translations.literal: Upon the death of his father he entered mourning; when mourning ended he was granted the honorific of bearing the imperial arms.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he entered mourning; after the mourning period he was granted the privilege of bearing the imperial arms.

sentences.zh: 久之，調荊鄂都統制、襄陽府駐劄，改沔州都統制。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to overall commander of Jing-E, garrisoned at Xiangyang Prefecture, then changed to overall commander of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was transferred to overall commander of Jing-E with his headquarters at Xiangyang Prefecture, and later reassigned as overall commander of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十二年，金人分道入蜀，犯湫池堡，又犯白環堡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiading, the Jin entered Shu by several routes, attacked the Qiuqi fort, and again attacked the Baihuan fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Jiading, the Jin invaded Shu by several routes, assaulted Qiuqi Fort, and then assaulted Baihuan Fort.

sentences.zh: 威部將石宣、董炤連卻之。

translations.literal: Wei's subordinate generals Shi Xuan and Dong Zhao repelled them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's lieutenants Shi Xuan and Dong Zhao drove them back in turn.

sentences.zh: 既而金人犯成州，威自西和退保仙人原。

translations.literal: Soon after the Jin attacked Chengzhou; Wei withdrew from Xihe to hold Xianren Plateau.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Jin struck Chengzhou, and Wei pulled back from Xihe to hold Xianren Plateau.

sentences.zh: 時興元都統制吳政戰死黃牛堡，李貴代政，亟走武休，金人已破武休，遂陷興元，又陷大安軍。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Zheng, overall commander of Xingyuan, died in battle at Huangniu Fort; Li Gui replaced Zheng and fled hastily to Wuxiu; the Jin had already broken Wuxiu, then took Xingyuan, and again took Da'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wu Zheng, overall commander of Xingyuan, had been killed at Huangniu Fort. Li Gui replaced him and fled headlong to Wuxiu. The Jin had already overrun Wuxiu, then seized Xingyuan, and went on to take Da'an Army.

sentences.zh: 先是，利州路安撫使丁焴聞金人深入，亟遣書招威東入救蜀，又檄忠義總管李好古北上捍禦。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ding Yu, pacification commissioner of Lizhou Circuit, hearing that the Jin had penetrated deeply, urgently sent letters summoning Wei eastward to rescue Shu, and also issued orders to the loyalist commander Li Haogu to advance north to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ding Yu, pacification commissioner of Lizhou Circuit, learning that the Jin had driven deep inland, had urgently written Wei to march east and relieve Shu, and also ordered the loyalist commander Li Haogu north to block them.

sentences.zh: 好古出魚關與統領張彪遇，以彪棄迷竹關故，斬之。

translations.literal: Haogu came out of Yugu Pass and met regimental commander Zhang Biao; because Biao had abandoned Mizhu Pass, he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Haogu came out through Yugu Pass and met the regimental commander Zhang Biao. Because Biao had abandoned Mizhu Pass, Haogu had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 彪，威弟也。

translations.literal: Biao was Wei's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was Wei's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 威聞彪死，按兵不進。

translations.literal: When Wei heard of Biao's death, he halted his army and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei learned that Biao had been killed, he halted his army and refused to move.

sentences.zh: 焴聞之，謂僚佐曰：「吳政身死，李貴復以兵敗，金人所憚惟威。

translations.literal: Yu heard of this and said to his staff: "Wu Zheng is dead, and Li Gui has again been defeated in battle; the only one the Jin fear is Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu heard of this, he told his staff, "Wu Zheng is dead, and Li Gui has been beaten again. The Jin fear no one but Wei.

sentences.zh: 今好古擅殺其弟，失威心，奈何？

translations.literal: Now Haogu has on his own authority killed his younger brother, losing Wei's goodwill — what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Now Haogu has killed his brother on his own authority and lost Wei's loyalty. What are we to do?

sentences.zh: 且金人在東，非威地分，今可無好古，不可無威。

translations.literal: Moreover the Jin are in the east, outside Wei's jurisdiction; we can do without Haogu now, but we cannot do without Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Jin are in the east, outside Wei's jurisdiction. We can spare Haogu, but we cannot spare Wei."

sentences.zh: 」遂因好古入見，數其擅殺彪罪，斬之。

translations.literal: He therefore had Haogu brought in on the pretext of meeting him, enumerated his crime of executing Biao on his own authority, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore had Haogu come in under pretense of an audience, charged him with executing Biao on his own authority, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 遣書速威進救蜀，且使進士田遂往說之。

translations.literal: He sent letters urging Wei to advance quickly to rescue Shu, and also sent jinshi graduate Tian Sui to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote urging Wei to hurry to Shu’s relief and sent the jinshi graduate Tian Sui to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 威感激，夜半調發，鼓行而前，破金人於金斗鎮。

translations.literal: Wei was deeply moved; at midnight he mobilized and marched forward with drums beating, crushing the Jin at Jindou Town.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this, Wei mobilized at midnight, marched forward to the beat of drums, and routed the Jin at Jindou Town.

sentences.zh: 金人雖敗未退，威頓兵不動，潛遣石宣等襲於大安軍，大破之。

translations.literal: Though the Jin were defeated they had not withdrawn; Wei held his army still, secretly sending Shi Xuan and others to strike at Da'an Army, inflicting a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Although beaten, the Jin had not retreated. Wei held his main force in place and secretly sent Shi Xuan and others to strike Da'an Army, inflicting a heavy defeat.

sentences.zh: 金人之來也，擇兩齒馬及精兵凡三千人，至是殲焉，俘其將巴土魯，大將包長壽聞之宵遁。

translations.literal: When the Jin had come they had selected three thousand two-toothed horses and elite troops; at this point they were annihilated; they captured the general Batu'er; the grand general Bao Changshou, hearing of this, fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin force that had come had been picked from three thousand prime horses and elite troops; now it was wiped out. They captured the general Batu'er, and the grand general Bao Changshou fled by night when he heard the news.

sentences.zh: 興元叛兵張福、莫簡作亂，以紅帕蒙首，號「紅巾隊」，焚利州，殺總領楊九鼎，破閬、果，入遂寧，遊騎在潼、漢界，將窺成都。

translations.literal: Rebel troops of Xingyuan, Zhang Fu and Mo Jian, raised a revolt; with red cloth bound over their heads they called themselves the Red Headband Corps; they burned Lizhou, killed commissioner Yang Jiuding, broke through Lang and Guo, entered Suining; their roaming cavalry reached the Tong and Han border, about to spy out Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu and Mo Jian, rebel soldiers from Xingyuan, rose in revolt. With red cloth bound over their heads they called themselves the Red Headband Corps. They burned Lizhou, killed the supply commissioner Yang Jiuding, overran Lang and Guo, entered Suining, and sent raiding parties to the Tong and Han frontier, poised to threaten Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 制置司謂賊勢欲西，非威不可禦。

translations.literal: The military commissionerate judged that the rebels' thrust was westward and that only Wei could repel them.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissionerate judged that the rebels meant to push west and that only Wei could stop them.

sentences.zh: 乃遣威提精兵六千人，自劍、綿至廣漢，盛夏暑劇，休士三日。

translations.literal: They dispatched Wei with six thousand elite troops; from Jian and Mian to Guanghan, in the height of summer with fierce heat, he rested his men for three days.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Wei with six thousand picked troops. From Jian and Mian to Guanghan, in the fierce heat of midsummer, he rested his men for three days.

sentences.zh: 俄安丙檄威東進，時賊自遂寧入普州茗山，威進兵重圍，絕其糧道，晝夜迫之。

translations.literal: Soon An Bing ordered Wei eastward; at that time the rebels from Suining entered Ming Mountain in Puzhou; Wei advanced with heavy encirclement, cut off their grain route, and pressed them day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Soon An Bing ordered Wei east. The rebels had left Suining and entered Ming Mountain in Puzhou. Wei advanced, tightened the encirclement, cut their supply lines, and pressed them day and night.

sentences.zh: 未幾禽福等十七人戮之，簡自殺，賊遂平。

translations.literal: Before long he captured Fu and seventeen others and executed them; Jian killed himself, and the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he captured Fu and seventeen others and executed them. Jian killed himself, and the rebellion was put down.

sentences.zh: 西夏來約夾攻金人，丙許之。

translations.literal: Western Xia came to propose a joint attack on the Jin; Bing agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia proposed a joint attack on the Jin, and Bing agreed.

sentences.zh: 遣王仕信會夏人於鞏，又命威與利帥程信、興帥陳立等分道並進。

translations.literal: He sent Wang Shixin to meet the Xia at Gong, and also ordered Wei together with Lizhou commander Cheng Xin, Xingyuan commander Chen Li, and others to advance by separate routes in concert.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Shixin to meet the Xia at Gong and ordered Wei, together with the Lizhou commander Cheng Xin, the Xingyuan commander Chen Li, and others, to advance by separate routes in concert.

sentences.zh: 威向秦州。

translations.literal: Wei marched toward Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei marched on Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 議初起，威謂：「金人尚強，夏人反覆，未可輕動。

translations.literal: When the plan was first raised, Wei said: "The Jin are still strong, and the Xia are fickle; we must not act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was first broached, Wei said, "The Jin are still strong and the Xia are unreliable. We must not move rashly."

sentences.zh: 」丙不聽，卒遣威，威黽勉而行，令所部毋得輕發，諸將至城下，無功而還。

translations.literal: Bing would not listen; in the end he dispatched Wei; Wei went reluctantly, ordering his command not to engage rashly; the generals reached the city walls and returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Bing would not listen and sent Wei anyway. Wei went reluctantly, ordering his troops not to engage lightly. The generals reached the city walls and came back empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 丙怒，奏罷其兵柄。

translations.literal: Bing was enraged and memorialized to strip him of military command.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Bing memorialized the throne to remove him from command.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒於利州，終揚州觀察使。

translations.literal: That year he died at Lizhou, his final rank being Yangzhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died at Lizhou, having reached the rank of Yangzhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 威初在行伍，以勇見稱，進充偏裨，每戰輒克，金人聞其名畏憚之。

translations.literal: Wei at first served in the ranks, famed for bravery; he advanced to company officer; in every battle he prevailed; the Jin, hearing his name, feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei began as an ordinary soldier, known for courage. He rose to company officer, won every battle he fought, and the Jin feared him at the mention of his name.

sentences.zh: 臨陳戰酣，則精采愈奮，兩眼皆赤，時號「張紅眼」，又號「張鶻眼」，威立「淨天鶻」旗以自表。

translations.literal: When battle grew fierce on the field his spirit burned even brighter; both eyes turned red; he was called Zhang Red-Eyes and also Zhang Hawk-Eyes; Wei raised the banner Pure Heaven Hawk as his emblem.
translations.idiomatic: In the heat of battle his spirit burned brighter still and both eyes turned red. Men called him "Zhang Red-Eyes" and also "Zhang Hawk-Eyes." He flew a banner reading "Pure Heaven Hawk" as his personal standard.

sentences.zh: 每戰不操它兵，有木棓號「紫大蟲」，圜而不刃，長不六尺，揮之掠陣，敵皆靡。

translations.literal: In every battle he used no other weapon; he had a wooden club called Purple Great Beast, round and without a blade edge, less than six chi long; wielding it he swept through the ranks and enemies all fell before him.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he used no other weapon. He carried a wooden club called "Purple Great Beast" — round, unedged, and less than six chi long. Swinging it through the ranks, he broke every enemy before him.

sentences.zh: 荊、鄂多平川廣野，威曰：「是彼騎兵之利也，鐵騎一衝，吾步技窮矣，蜀中戰法不可用。

translations.literal: Jing and E have many broad plains; Wei said: "That is where their cavalry excel; once iron cavalry charges, our infantry tactics are exhausted; Shu battle methods cannot be used here."
translations.idiomatic: Jing and E are mostly open plain, and Wei said, "That plays to their cavalry. One charge of iron horsemen and our infantry tactics are spent. The fighting methods of Shu will not work here."

sentences.zh: 」乃意創法，名「撒星陳」，分合不常，聞鼓則聚，聞金則散。

translations.literal: He therefore devised a new formation called Scattered Stars Array, irregular in splitting and joining; at the sound of drums they gathered, at the sound of gongs they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore devised a new formation he called the Scattered Stars Array, shifting between dispersion and concentration without fixed pattern: at the drum they gathered, at the gong they scattered.

sentences.zh: 騎兵至則聲金，一軍分為數十簇；

translations.literal: When cavalry arrived they sounded the gong and one army split into dozens of clusters;
translations.idiomatic: When enemy cavalry appeared, he sounded the gong and one body of troops split into dozens of clusters;

sentences.zh: 金人隨而分兵，則又鼓而聚之。

translations.literal: the Jin followed by dividing their forces, then they beat drums again to reassemble.
translations.idiomatic: the Jin divided in pursuit, whereupon he beat the drums and drew his men together again.

sentences.zh: 倏忽之間，分合數變，金人失措，然後縱擊之，以此輒勝。

translations.literal: In an instant they split and joined several times; the Jin were thrown into confusion, then they were unleashed to strike — by this means they always won.
translations.idiomatic: In moments the formation split and re-formed several times. The Jin lost their footing, and then he let his men charge. By this method he won again and again.

sentences.zh: 威御軍紀律嚴整，兵行常若銜枚，罕聞其聲。

translations.literal: Wei commanded troops with strict discipline; on the march they were like men with gag-sticks in their mouths, rarely heard.
translations.idiomatic: Wei kept iron discipline. On the march his men moved as if gagged with wooden sticks — scarcely a sound was heard.

sentences.zh: 每與百姓避路，買食物則賈倍於市，迄無敢喧。

translations.literal: They always yielded the road to common people; when buying food they paid double the market price, and no one ever dared make a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: They always gave way to civilians on the road. When they bought food they paid twice the market price, and no one dared raise a commotion.

sentences.zh: 晚以嗜欲多疾，故不壽云。

translations.literal: In his later years excessive indulgence brought many illnesses, and therefore he did not live long, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years excess and indulgence brought many illnesses, and so, it is said, he did not live long.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋之南渡，邊將之才何其鮮哉！

translations.literal: Commentary says: After the Song crossed south, how sparse were the talents of frontier generals!
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: After the Song crossed south, how few talented frontier generals there were!

sentences.zh: 或曰「江南非用武之地」，然古之善兵者，若孫武子，亦吳人也。

translations.literal: Some say the lands south of the Yangtze are no place for wielding arms, yet among ancient masters of war, Sun Wu himself was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that lands south of the Yangtze are no field for arms, yet Sun Wu, among the ancients who excelled at war, was himself a man of Wu.

sentences.zh: 抑先王之世，文武無二道，文武既分，宜其才之各有所偏勝也。

translations.literal: Perhaps in the age of former kings, civil and military were not two paths; once civil and military were divided, it is fitting that talents should each excel in their own bias.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps in the age of the former kings civil and military were not two separate paths. Once they were split apart, it is only natural that talent should lean one way or the other.

sentences.zh: 趙方少從張栻學、許國之忠，應變之略，隱然有尊俎折衝之風。

translations.literal: Zhao Fang in youth studied under Zhang Shi; in Xu Guo's loyalty and adaptability in strategy, he quietly bore the air of conducting diplomacy from the banquet hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fang studied under Zhang Shi in his youth. Like Xu Guo's loyalty and his gift for adapting to events, he quietly carried the bearing of a man who could settle affairs over the banquet table.

sentences.zh: 其部曲如扈再興、孟宗政後皆為名將，亦方之能獎率也。

translations.literal: His subordinates such as Hu Zaixing and Meng Zongzheng later all became famous generals — also Fang's ability to encourage and lead.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates such as Hu Zaixing and Meng Zongzheng later became famous generals in their own right — a measure also of Fang's power to inspire and lead.

sentences.zh: 方之子范、葵，宗政子珙，後皆以功名自見，不愧其父，有足稱者。

translations.literal: Fang's sons Fan and Kui, and Zongzheng's son Gong, later all distinguished themselves through merit and fame, not shaming their fathers — worthy of mention.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's sons Fan and Kui, and Zongzheng's son Gong, later won distinction in their own right and did not disgrace their fathers — all worth noting.

sentences.zh: 賈涉居方面，亦號有才，及其庶孽，竟至亡國，為可歎也。

translations.literal: Jia She held a frontier post and was also reputed talented, yet his bastard offspring in the end brought the state to ruin — a matter for lament.
translations.idiomatic: Jia She too held a frontier command and was counted talented, yet his illegitimate son in the end helped ruin the state — a thing to sigh over.

sentences.zh: 張威者善於御眾，故所至立功云。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei was skilled at commanding troops, and therefore wherever he went he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei was skilled at leading men, and so wherever he was sent he won distinction.
